long_biography.plain_text:
The purchase of Brahma turned Jorge Paulo Lemann's acquisition discipline towards consumer brands. He and his partners combined the brewer with regional rivals, formed Ambev and then joined it with Interbrew. The later purchase of Anheuser-Busch created the global beer group that became his largest identifiable asset.

Lemann carried that model into 3G Capital, using concentrated ownership, operational involvement and debt-backed transactions to acquire established companies. Burger King and Heinz extended the approach beyond brewing; more recent investments include Hunter Douglas and Skechers. Although management has passed to newer partners, 3G still describes itself as a private partnership built around an owner-operator approach.
